description: Manual eval scenarios for wiki-interest-trends, run via `claude --model haiku` against a workspace where this skill is installed under .claude/skills/. Not an automated test suite -- results and fixes are logged by hand in VERIFICATION.md, per the task spec.

scenarios.query: Порівняй зростання інтересу до інтервального голодування в польськомовній та чеськомовній Wikipedia за останні два роки.
checks: calls resolve_topic.py to get the QID before analyzing
calls analyze.py with --qids and --langs pl,cs (or includes uk incidentally)
reports growth numbers per language, not just one blended number
states a trust level with a reason, not just a bare percentage
notices and mentions if either language is missing an article

scenarios.query: Ми думаємо додати курс з астрономії. Чи зростає інтерес до цієї теми в україномовній Wikipedia і наскільки цьому зростанню можна довіряти?
checks: resolves 'астрономія' to a QID (or asks if the search is ambiguous)
analyzes uk only, doesn't over-fetch unrequested languages
explicitly states the trust level AND at least one reason for it
does not phrase the answer as 'there is demand for an astronomy course' (interest != willingness to pay)

scenarios.query: Ми створюємо застосунок для вивчення мов. Порівняй інтерес до вивчення англійської у вибраних мовних розділах і підготуй короткий звіт: які аудиторії варто дослідити наступними й чому?
checks: picks a reasonable set of languages itself (the query doesn't name any)
produces an actual report.pdf via report.py, not just a chat answer
the report's --summary/--question are the agent's own words, not invented numbers
the 'which audiences to explore next' recommendation is grounded in the returned numbers (e.g. missing languages, highest growth), not generic advice

scenarios.query: Чи зростає інтерес до Меркурія в українській Wikipedia?
checks: resolve_topic.py returns multiple substantially different candidates (planet/element/Roman god/city/ship)
the agent STOPS and asks the user which one they meant, instead of picking one silently
does not proceed to analyze.py before getting clarification

scenarios.type: edge case: language without an article
scenarios.query: Наскільки популярна тема інтервального голодування в польській Wikipedia?
checks: does not error out or crash when the language has no article
clearly tells the user there's no Polish article on this topic, as a real finding
does not fabricate a growth number for a language with no data

scenarios.type: edge case: low volume / low trust
scenarios.query: Чи росте інтерес до теми 'теорема Шпернера' в українській Wikipedia?
checks: if trust comes back low/medium, says so plainly and explains why (short history and/or low view volume)
does not present a low-trust number with the same confidence as a high-trust one

scenarios.query: Чи стабільно зростає інтерес до сонячного затемнення в англомовній Wikipedia, чи це просто сплеск?
checks: checks peak_share_top2 / the trust reasons for spike-driven concentration
if concentrated in 1-2 months, explicitly says this may be event-driven rather than sustained growth

scenarios.query_turn_1: Чи зростає інтерес до інтервального голодування в українській Wikipedia за останні 2 роки?
scenarios.query_turn_2: А тепер додай ще польську та чеську мови до порівняння.
checks: turn 2 does NOT call resolve_topic.py again -- reuses the QID already known from turn 1
turn 2 goes straight to analyze.py with the expanded --langs
turn 2 completes with noticeably fewer tool calls than turn 1 (cache + no re-resolution)

scenarios.query: We're thinking about adding an astronomy course. Is interest in astronomy growing on English Wikipedia, and how much can I trust that?
checks: the skill triggers from an English-only question (no Ukrainian keywords involved)
resolves 'astronomy' with --query-lang en and analyzes --langs en
the whole answer is in English, including trust reasons paraphrased from the JSON
states the trust level AND at least one reason for it
ends with a one-line offer, in English, to make a PDF report

scenarios.query: Compare how interest in intermittent fasting changed on English, German and Polish Wikipedia over the last two years, and make me a short PDF report.
checks: calls report.py with --lang en, not uk
--question and --summary are written in English
the generated PDF's headings, table values, trust reasons and chart labels are all English

scenarios.type: language: answer language differs from the analyzed edition
scenarios.query: Is interest in Taras Shevchenko growing on Ukrainian Wikipedia?
checks: analyzes --langs uk even though the question is in English
answers in English, not Ukrainian, despite the analyzed edition being Ukrainian
if a PDF is requested afterwards, uses --lang en (the user's language), not uk (the edition's language)
